safety_lead_time.comparison_action: reduce from SAP 4.0 days to recommended 1.83 days

narrative: Material PL1__M04181E6 displays smooth, near-continuous demand (CV=0.16, mean 115,500 units/day) with no stockouts across 87 observed working days. Supplier lead times are highly variable (CV=0.58, range 0.05–3.97 days), making lead time uncertainty the dominant risk factor. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy with an EOQ-derived order quantity of 1,077,870 units and a combined-variance safety stock of 211,155 units is selected to achieve the 95% service level while reducing annual costs by 61.7% through order consolidation.

research_insights.selected_model: (r, Q) continuous-review with EOQ order quantity
research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is smooth and near-continuous (CV=0.16), satisfying EOQ assumptions. The fixed reorder point naturally handles the unstable lead times through the combined-variance safety stock formula, avoiding over-complexity.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage utilisation is 51.6% (1,289,025 of 2,500,438 units). The capacity constraint does not bind and no order quantity reduction is required.
